newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INSTANT VIEW-Portugal CPI rises 0.1 pct in Dec.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Portugal CPI rises 0.1 pct in Dec.

text.p: The following are quick reactions by analysts to news that Portugal's Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent in December, in line with forecasts.
JORGE FERRAZ, IMF - INFORMACAO DE MERCADOS FINANCEIROS

"A first response of the Bank of Portugal could be a 20 basis point cut in the drain rate on Friday. It is going to wait for the next Bundesbank meeting next week before cutting the repo rate. It is unlikely to cut the repo rate owing, on the one hand, to the lack of news about the Bundesbank's intentions, and on the other, to the fact that the December inflation was slightly above expectations."
(Analysts' forecasts for December inflation had ranged from unchanged to a rise of 0.2 percent month-on-month).
JOAO LOURENCO, SIEMCA-SOCIEDADE MEDIADORA DE CAPITAIS

"They are not particularly positive figures but they are what was expected and so I don't think there will be much market reaction. The year-on-year rose because last year (December 1995) was very low. December is traditionally an inflationary month. With these numbers I believe the Bank of Portugal is not going to touch rates. It cut last week because of the escudo.

"It was in line with expectations. The rise in the year-on-year rate is due to the fact that (the monthly) rate was negative in (December) 1995. I don't know if the Bank will cut on Friday. It is going to depend on the escudo.
